title: Normalized local complete-intersection adjunction systems
statement:
Let $p:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], and $d\geq0$. Work simultaneously over all cartesian base-change records $B$ [def-sfb-flat-lci-base-change]. A polynomial presentation of relative rank $d$ on an open $U\subset X$ consists of integers $n,c$ with $n=c+d$, an open immersion $P\to\mathbb A^n_S$ [def-sbc-affine-space], [def-weil-open-immersion], and a closed immersion $i:U\to P$ [def-weil-closed-immersion] whose composite is $p|_U$. At every point of $U$, the ideal of $i$ is generated on an ambient affine neighbourhood by $c$ equations which form a regular sequence after localization at every prime containing the ideal [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence]. Put $A=i^*\mathcal I_i$ and $V=i^*\Omega^1_{P/S}$, where module pullback and differentials are [def-pc-module-pullback], [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials]. The presentation line is $D(A,V)=(\bigwedge^c A)^\vee\otimes\bigwedge^n V$, using sheaf exterior powers [def-sc-sheaf-exterior-power]. The conormal differential is characterized on ideal sections by $[s]\mapsto ds$, and the source differential by $1\otimes da\mapsto d(i^\sharp a)$.

An adjunction system consists of an invertible module $L_B$ [def-sc-invertible-module] for every $B$, comparisons $D(A_C,V_C)\simeq L_B|_U$ for every presentation $C$ of $p_B$, and comparisons $g^*L_B\simeq L_D$ for every cartesian arrow $(g,b):D\to B$ commuting with the maps to $p$. The identity comparison is the normalized tensor-pullback identity; the comparison for a composite is the normalized tensor-pullback composition followed by the pullback of the first comparison and then the second comparison.

Normalized refinements and pullbacks of presentations carry the actual maps on ideal sections (induced by the ideal inclusions) and on universal differentials (induced by derivation), not arbitrary module maps. On a refinement with two-term maps $f:A\to B$, $g:V\to W$ and differentials $d_A,d_B$, the determinant comparison is the kernel-first exact-cone comparison. More explicitly, if $a,b,n,m$ are the four ranks with $a+m=b+n$, choose ordered bases of $A,B,V,W$ and dual conormal orientations taking the basis wedges to $1$. Choose lifts $l_j$ of the basis of $W$ under $(d_B,g):B\oplus V\to W$, and let $M$ be the matrix of the ordered columns $(f(a_i),-d_A(a_i))$ followed by $l_j$, in the ordered basis of $B\oplus V$. A comparison $e:D(A,V)\simeq D(B,W)$ is normalized when $d_Ag=fd_B$ and $\det(M)e(\rho_A\otimes\mathrm{vol}_V)=(-1)^{a(b+1)}\rho_B\otimes\mathrm{vol}_W$. This equation is used on every open and every such choice, so it also applies over rings with zero divisors and to rank zero. For pullbacks of presentations, conormal and differential maps are isomorphisms, and the determinant comparison sends each pulled-back dual-conormal tensor volume orientation to the corresponding orientation, with the ranks transported by their specified equalities.

The predicate IsNormalized requires the unique conormal/source differential maps in every presentation; existence of normalized refinements for every ambient morphism preserving the closed source and structural map; existence of normalized presentation pullbacks for every cartesian closed-source square whose ambient square is cartesian or an open restriction with etale base map [def-weil-etale-morphism]; the displayed exact-cone normalization of every transition between local comparisons; and the displayed pullback-orientation normalization of the local comparison induced by every global base-change map. These are properties of a supplied system, with no existence theorem, no Noetherian hypothesis, and no geometric finiteness assumption on $p$ or on the new bases.
